transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I feel like I’m just always moving from one thing to the next. I really can’t just sit idle. And... well, we have a new work setup at my job, and it's made that constant moving around a lot harder to hide.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks?

Yeah, I do. Especially at work. Like in those longer coaching meetings we have, or when I have to sit and read through a new procedure. I'll start off fine, but after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes just kept moving and... well, I didn't actually take in a single thing that was said or written down.
Do you often fidget or squirm when you have to sit still?

Yeah, I do. Even when I’m really trying to just sit there and look calm, my foot is usually bouncing under the desk. Or I'll be clicking a pen during one of those meetings and... well, I do it without really noticing it until I catch myself.
Do you often find yourself interrupting other people?

Yeah, I do that too. I don't mean to be rude, but... well, if I hear my coworkers working through a customer problem, I'll just jump right in with the answer before they've even finished talking, or... before anyone even asked me for help. I just kind of blurt it out.
Do you also often lose things you need for tasks, like keys, paperwork, or your phone?

No, not really. I mean, I guess everyone misplaces their phone once in a while, but... no, I usually know where my stuff is. I've always got a specific spot for my keys at home, and at work, my papers and headset just stay right there on my desk. So I wouldn't say losing things is really an issue for me.
Do you often leave your seat when you’re expected to stay seated?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, with my job, I'm on the phone a lot, so I pretty much have to stay glued to my headset. I might bounce my leg like I mentioned earlier, but... no, I don't actually get up and walk around when I'm supposed to be working. I just stay put.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high, expansive, or irritable for several days in a row?

No, I can't say I have. I mean, sure, I get a little irritable if it's been a long day on the phones, but... no, nothing like being unusually high or, you know, feeling like that for days at a time. My mood is pretty steady, really.
Do you often make careless mistakes because you miss details?

Yeah, I do actually. At work, I’ll... I'll think I’ve completely finished a customer ticket, and then later on I notice I typed the wrong account number. Or maybe I skipped a required box on the screen. It's usually just missing one little instruction, but it makes the whole thing come back to me to fix. So, yeah, that happens.
Do you often feel restless or driven to keep moving even when you’re expected to stay still?

Yeah, I do get that feeling. If I have to sit still through a training video for work, or maybe a slow appointment, I start to feel kind of boxed in. It's like I really need to stand up and stretch, or just... do something with my hands. I don't always get up, like I said before, but that restless feeling is definitely there.
Do you often get distracted by noises or other things happening around you when you’re trying to focus?

Yeah, definitely. Working from home or even in the office, there's just so much going on. I'll have the chat window open for a customer, the CRM system pulled up, and then our team messages going off. If I hear one beep from a message, or if someone's talking nearby, it just... it pulls me right off track. I'll completely lose my place with the customer I was helping and have to figure out where we left off.
Do you often feel like you can’t stay seated, even when you’re expected to?

No, not really. I mean, I feel that restless feeling I mentioned a minute ago, but I don't actually get up. I know I'm supposed to stay in my seat when I'm on the clock or in a meeting, so I just stay put. I might tap my foot or fidget, but I don't feel like I absolutely can't stay seated.
Do you often leave your seat when you’re expected to stay seated?

No, I don't really do that. Like I said just a second ago, I know I need to stay in my chair when I'm working or in a meeting. I might feel a bit antsy, but I don't actually get up and walk away when I'm supposed to be sitting.
Do you often feel like you need to run about or climb on things when you’re supposed to stay calm or still?

No, I don't run around or climb on things. I'm 57, so that's not really something I do. But... I do get this feeling sometimes, like if I have to sit still through a long training video for work, or if things are just really slow. I start feeling kind of boxed in, you know? Like I just need to stand up, or stretch my legs, or at least do something with my hands because just sitting there doing nothing makes me feel too restless.
Do you often talk too much?

No, I wouldn't say so. I talk to customers all day for my job, but I just stick to the script and answer their questions. I don't really go off on tangents or talk people's ears off in my regular life, either. I pretty much just say what I need to say.
Before age 15, did you often get into trouble for breaking rules or acting aggressively, like fighting, stealing, lying, or destroying things?
No, I didn't do any of that. I was a pretty normal kid, really. I wasn't getting into fights or stealing things or anything like that. I mostly just stayed out of trouble.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble paying attention in school?

Yeah, actually. Looking back, I realize this has been around long before any recent job changes. Back in grade school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. They'd say I talked out of turn, and that I constantly had to be reminded to just stay with my work. So, yeah, paying attention was definitely an issue back then.
As a child, did you often fidget, squirm, or have trouble sitting still when you were supposed to be quiet or seated?
No, not really. I mean, I don't remember being particularly squirmy or anything. I don't think I had any more trouble sitting still than the next kid.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble waiting your turn?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't remember having any real issues with waiting my turn or anything like that back then.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble staying seated when you were expected to?

No, I don't remember that being a problem. I mean, I stayed in my desk just fine. My mind might have been wandering off, but I wasn't getting up and walking around the classroom when I wasn't supposed to.
